function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for the command execution time, such as 'seconds' or 'milliseconds'

But the user says "timeout 10". Maybe they want to run "timeout 10" which might not be correct. But we can interpret that they want to run "timeout 10" as a command. We need to use the function to execute a system command. The function is cmd_controller_execute. We need to pass the command string "timeout 10". Also specify unit? The function signature: command: string, unit?: "seconds" | "milliseconds". The default is N/A. We can just pass command: "timeout 10". That will run the command. But we need to consider that the environment might not support "timeout" command. But we can still call it. The function will execute the command. We should call the function.
